prompt: A ride-hailing company's share in one city fell from 60% to 45% in six months after a rival cut prices 20%. The company's own prices were unchanged. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: Price-sensitive riders are likely switching to the rival.
options.feedback: Right. It commits to a likely cause that fits the facts, and it is testable: I'd compare share loss by trip type and time of day, where price matters most.

options.text: It could be prices, wait times, driver supply, promotions or app ratings.
options.feedback: This lists several causes without committing to the most likely one.

options.text: Price is the only factor, so the company must match the 20% cut immediately.
options.feedback: This states a cause as certain before any data has tested it.
This is too vague to test: it doesn't say what is wrong or what data would show it.

explanation: Share loss timed with a rival's price cut suggests price sensitivity. Where share fell most tests it.

distractor_flaws.M.shotgun_hypotheses: It could be prices, wait times, driver supply, promotions or app ratings.
distractor_flaws.M.overconfident_hypothesis: Price is the only factor, so the company must match the 20% cut immediately.
